objective: Review everything produced so far (Gradle/Spring Boot dependency setup, backend agents, CI/CD) and apply only the changes that are strictly needed for it to be correct and consistent with its sources of authority. The only change needed is in README.md, where the Tecnologías section still names Maven/mvnw/pom.xml although the build uses the Gradle 9.8.0 wrapper required by the stack. Adding an HTTP/web starter is a blocker because the documentation repository has not made that decision.

decisions.decision: MODIFY README.md lines 36 and 38 only. The stack (docs/stack.md, Backend table: 'Gradle | 9.8.0') is the authority on the build tool. The repository has gradlew, gradle/wrapper (distributionUrl gradle-9.8.0-bin.zip) and build.gradle, and has no mvnw or pom.xml. The README's own CI/CD section already says to run ./gradlew, so the README currently contradicts itself and tells developers to use files that do not exist. This change does not touch the user's edits: the Java rows on line 34 ('25 (LTS) o superior') and line 42 ('JDK 25 o superior') stay exactly as they are.

Do not change `version` in build.gradle or `sonar.projectVersion`. Per AGENTS.md 'Configuration', a version bump is required only when a configuration file, or a file referenced by a configuration section, changes. Neither changes here: the README text is documentation, not configuration.

Do not add spring-boot-starter-webmvc, spring-boot-starter-webflux or any embedded server. The stack's Backend table names Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA, Spring Data MongoDB, Spring AMQP, Spring Security, JUnit, Mockito and Testcontainers, but no web/HTTP module. Request 1 was limited to 'only the backend dependencies of the documented stack'. Choosing servlet (WebMVC) or reactive (WebFlux), and which server, is a stack decision owned by FMAT-Restaurant/Menu-Documentation. It is recorded as a blocker. The check found that the bootJar has spring-web 7.0.9 (brought in transitively) but no Tomcat, Jetty, Undertow or reactor-netty server.

Keep `EXPOSE 8080` in the Dockerfile. EXPOSE is only image metadata and does not open or require a port. It matches the HTTP interface of the accepted API contract (docs/contracts/api-contract.md, 'Raíz del API: /api/v1') and Spring Boot's default port. Removing it now and adding it back once the web-stack blocker is resolved would be churn.

Rejected, with no write: (a) the README 'Documentación relacionada' reference to 'output/ers/spec.md', which does not exist in the docs repository. It is user-authored text from before these requests, and fixing it would be unrelated broken-reference repair. (b) The README Java row wording 'o superior' / 'compatible hasta Java 26'. This is the user's own edit and does not contradict the Java 25 toolchain, because foojay provisions Temurin 25. (c) The agent definitions (.agents/agents/*, .codex/agents/*.toml). They match the docs-repo reference plus backend adaptations, and every relative link resolves. (d) ci.yml, sonar-project.properties, checkstyle.xml and the Testcontainers images. They are verified correct (see VERIFY entries), and the image tags match the stack: postgres 18.6, mongo 8.3.11, rabbitmq 4.3.6, eclipse-temurin 25.0.4.1.

blockers: WEB-STACK: The accepted API contract (docs/contracts/api-contract.md, 'Raíz del API: /api/v1') defines an HTTP interface, but docs/stack.md lists no web module (Spring Web MVC or WebFlux) and no embedded server. The current bootJar has no HTTP server, so the Docker image published by CD cannot serve the contract and EXPOSE 8080 has nothing behind it. Adding a web starter would deviate from the stack and from request 1 ('only the dependencies of the documented stack'). FMAT-Restaurant/Menu-Documentation must add the web technology and version to stack.md before this repository adds it. This does not block the current review: nothing implemented so far depends on it.
